title: GPM: Meet the Team: Carlton Peters
description: This is a series of short profiles that showcase the systems engineers and designers who helped develop, build, and test the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Core Observatory spacecraft.
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: I'm definitely looking forward to launch.
This will actually be the first mission that I've gotten to see, kind of from the PD-R
timeframe, preliminary design, timeframe, all the way through to launch.
We basically deal with the day-to-day activities in I-T, and we are wrapping up a lot of our
We performed our thermal vac test, which is our big thermal test, kind of out of sequence
Usually it's the last of the environmental test.
The thermal vac test involves pretty much every subsystem.
It's the biggest, most involved test.
It ran for roughly a month and a half.
The challenge of doing it first is that as we move forward in our other environmental
tests, not necessarily disturbing the integrity of our thermal design as we move forward
and have to change some things on the spacecraft.
Once we get on orbit and we start getting data and all the science information comes back
and all the thermal design comes in and things look great, that'll be a great rewarding experience.
